_comment: The G.2 decision rule, frozen 2026-08-27, before either option was
scored against it. Same discipline as extraction/TOLERANCES.json: a
rule written after seeing which option wins is a description, not a
rule. Its SHA-256 is recorded in chip/g2_decision.py, in
--freeze-check in CI requires all four to agree.
The hard constraints are evaluated against numbers measured in E.1a
and E.1b. The declared inputs below are estimates, and they are in
this file rather than in the script so that they are frozen with the
rule instead of chosen alongside the answer.

committed._comment: The standard tile figure is from the info.yaml comment and is used only to express the die as a ratio. The authority on how many tiles are bought is the tiles string itself.

hard.name: fits the free row area with a quarter of it still in reserve
hard.why: E.1a's free figure counts all decap as reclaimable and the power question behind that is open. A reserve absorbs being wrong about it.

hard.name: needs no tile beyond the 2x2 already committed
hard.why: A fifth tile is roughly 70 euro and, more to the point, changes the floorplan and forces a full re-harden.

hard.name: leaves both existing arms at sixteen oscillators each
hard.why: E.1's own checklist: preserve the two-arm result rather than sacrificing it for a small third sample.

hard.name: gives the new arm at least eight independent oscillators
hard.why: E.1's stated floor for a comparison worth making.

hard.name: costs at most one new input pin
hard.why: ui[7] is the only free input. Everything past it has to come out of uio[1:7], which E.2 is spending.

hard.name: builds in at most five working days
hard.why: The chip path is 17 to 23 working days against a shuttle that opens in September. A build longer than a week eats the margin that exists so G.3 can re-run the whole evidence suite.

preference_order: answers the countermeasure question: can an open automated flow suppress layout leakage with constraints, or does it need a hard macro
gives a causal calibration curve for extraction-to-frequency prediction
lower risk that the flow cannot deliver the treatment at all

declared_inputs._comment: Estimates, frozen with the rule. Each says what it rests on.

armc.build_days_basis: Placement and routing equalization constraints in OpenLane, then one build per candidate constraint set until the ring bounding boxes match. Two days of constraint writing, two of iteration.
armc.delivery_risk_basis: The open flow has no supported way to force sixteen identical placements. It is the point of the experiment and it is also the thing that might not work.

ladder.build_days_basis: Generated RTL, no placement constraint, one build. The generator is a variation on dualarm/gen_dualarm.py, which already emits sixteen instances.
ladder.delivery_risk_basis: Nothing about it depends on the flow doing something unusual.
